summary: Frontend smoke test of stale-cache fix on paras reward preview. All 6 scenarios pass on the preview env: first load renders landing hero, hard-reload renders cleanly, /how-it-works and /faq lazy chunks load, /login page mounts with input fields and accepts keystrokes, no ChunkLoadError/Unexpected-token-< in console, and localStorage.paras_force_refresh_v10 is no longer set on first visit. Original infinite-spinner bug only manifests on real Cloudflare-cached prod traffic and cannot be reproduced on preview — verification scope was regression-only as instructed.

critical_code_review_comments: index.js still has lots of dead service-worker code (preserved behind early `return`) — fine for now but could be deleted in a follow-up cleanup.

index.html has THREE watchdogs at 5s/15s/20s plus index.js reloadOnce throttle (20s) plus App.js Suspense watchdog (12s) — these can fight each other on genuinely slow networks. Throttles guard against loops, but worth tracking real-world behaviour.

Aggressive 5s watchdog (WATCHDOG_MS=5000) is fine for desktops but may fire spuriously on 2G/very-slow-mobile users who haven't finished JS download in 5s. Recommend instrumenting `[self-heal] triggered: watchdog-5s …` warnings via WebVitalsReporter to see how often it fires in prod.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Cache/recovery fix tested on preview. Bug is only reproducible against real Cloudflare-cached prod traffic — preview confirms the fix does not regress normal load/refresh/lazy-route behaviour. If retesting, focus on real prod behaviour after the next deploy: clear browsing data → load www.parasreward.com → refresh → confirm no infinite spinner.
rca of the issue: Original bug: stale cached index.html referenced hashed /static/js/*.chunk.js paths that no longer exist on server after a deploy. Emergent's static host falls back to index.html (HTML, not 404) for missing paths → browser parses HTML as JS → ChunkLoadError/'Unexpected token <'. Prior recovery used window.location.reload() which still hit the same HTTP cache and the same poisoned HTML → infinite spinner once 30s throttle was hit. Fix replaces reload() with window.location.replace(url+'?_cb='+ts) so the URL is unique and bypasses HTTP/CDN cache, plus removes the conflicting `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000` meta tag, adds a 20s Suspense-stuck watchdog, and removes the FORCE_REFRESH_MARKER_v10 unconditional reload that compounded the bad UX after clearing browsing data.
